requirements.verifier_assertion: The program is invoked as: python solution.py --input /app/inputs/pages --output /app/result.json; every *.html in the input directory is processed.
Each .html file is rewritten in place with its sanitized version; the report is written to /app/result.json.
The allowed tag set is exactly the listed tags (case-insensitive); any tag not in the list is not allowed.
Non-allowed tags are unwrapped: tag removed but inner text and already-sanitized children preserved; each unwrap increments removed_tags.
must_include: inner text and already-sanitized children are preserved

requirements.verifier_assertion: a keeps only href and title; img keeps only src, alt, title; meta keeps only charset, name, content; every other allowed tag keeps no attributes; removed attrs increment stripped_attributes.
must_include: the a element keeps only href and title
every other allowed tag keeps NO attributes

requirements.verifier_assertion: href/src values starting with javascript:, vbscript:, or data:text/html are dropped (element kept); data:image/... is preserved; each drop increments blocked_urls.
Text node content is never altered; dangerous-looking substrings inside text nodes must remain verbatim.
result.json is a JSON object with a single key files whose value is an array sorted ascending by file name; output must be deterministic (byte-identical on re-run).
Each entry has exactly: name, status, removed_tags, stripped_attributes, blocked_urls.
status is unchanged when all counts are 0 (empty file also unchanged), sanitized when any count is non-zero, error when the file cannot be read or parsed.
must_include: an empty file is also unchanged
sanitized when at least one tag, attribute, or URL was changed
error when the file cannot be read or parsed
